src.label: Cyprus Veterinary Services (Ministry of Agriculture) — entry of pet animals into the Republic of Cyprus

head: Pets must be at least 105 days old; from outside the EU they need an animal health certificate and sometimes a titre test.
lines: Cyprus bans entry of any unvaccinated dog, cat or ferret. The microchip must come first, the primary rabies shot at 12 weeks or older, and 21 days must pass before travel, so every animal must be at least 105 days old on entry.

From a third country the pet needs the prescribed Animal Health Certificate plus the owner's declaration that the move is non-commercial. If the country is not on the EU list of countries exempt from titration, a rabies antibody test of at least 0.5 IU/ml is required, sampled at least 30 days after a primary vaccination and three months before the certificate is issued, in an EU-designated lab.

The page explains that origin is where the journey began, not a country you merely pass through. A stop in an unlisted country can be treated as transit only if the pet had no contact with rabies-susceptible animals and stayed secured in the vehicle or the airport's international area.
